item.title: The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana (August 2026)
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|competitive

The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana (August 2026)

All Vine, All the time.

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Sep 4, 2026

|

7 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The Disney Lorcana North American Championship is in our rear-view mirror and yet another month is sunsetting for the market at large. We're officially in year four for Disney Lorcana. How absurd is that?! I've been writing articles here on TCGplayer since The First Chapter and it doesn't feel even close to that long.

In that time, the Disney Lorcana ecosystem has evolved multiple times. We've seen eras dominated by playables, and others where collectability is king. In fact, it's safe to say that the recent boom in attention has come more so from those big-ticket items. That's led to some speculation that the playability of Disney Lorcana is on a downswing...

...so let me tell you that's utter nonsense. 

I have the pleasure of diving into the numbers here at TCGplayer roughly once a month. Make no mistake: transactions are trending upwards overall, but the majority of those increases can be found in under-$5 must-haves that have rocked a recent tournament. August may have been the biggest example of that in recent memory — not a single card in our top ten currently retails for more than $10 a copy. 

The North American Championship has set the status quo, but the European Championship is quickly coming around the bend. If we see a similar level of commanding performance across the pond, I would expect multiple of these price tags to jump as supply begins to disappear. As a result, it's a good time to be buying in... but what exactly are y'all buying into? 

I've crunched the numbers for you. Let's take a look at the best-selling Disney Lorcana cards throughout August 2026. Spoiler: It's Attack of the Vine! All of the time. 

#10 Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends

We said it back when Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends was revealed: if Amber Steel is good, you're slamming four copies of this thing. 

Whispers were going around prior to the event, but Joseph Quigley's breakout performance at the North American Championship solidified all doubt of that. Amber Steel is a potent choice if you're looking for counterplay into some of the most popular archetypes in the room right now and Lilo & Stitch are sitting at the helm of that. 

At $2.50? Don't mind if I do. 

#9 Paradise Falls - Exotic Destination

Needless to say, Emerald Steel absolutely dominated at the North American Championship. The deck managed to capture six spots in the top eight and truly stands as the deck to beat right now. The thing is? They've just moved away from the variants of the deck playing Paradise Falls - Exotic Destination. 

Previously, players looked to the location from Attack of the Vine! alongside Touch the Sky in order to draw a fresh fist full of cards. That's still quite powerful, but it's not where you want to be in a room stuffed with both the mirror match and Amber Emerald. 

Will it come back into fashion? Hard to say. I won't pretend it isn't damn cool though. 

#8 Violet Parr - Super Resilient

Honestly, it's a similar story for Violet Parr - Super Resilient. This card had a barnburner of a start to the month as a lynchpin of multiple Amethyst Steel strategies... all of which have begun to underperform as the format has evolved. 

That's not because the card is bad, though. Far from it. Violet is hard to remove and provides potent card selection to any deck capable of shifting her. She's also a spectacular singer for more expensive songs thanks to her shift ability. As a result, I'm fully expecting her to make a comeback as the metagame shifts back in her favor. 

#7 Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends

Ruby Amethyst kind of appeared out of nowhere to steal the CCS $50k Invitational event last month. Garrett Martin prided himself on cooking up a list that had game into Emerald Steel, Amber Emerald and Amber Amethyst — complete with two copies of Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends. 

Playing with (and answering) Evasive characters has quickly become one of the more important aspects of the format and Peter Pan & Tinker Bell - Fast Friends can not only do so itself, but allows any other character to step up to the challenge as well. It also incidentally serves as an activator for Vixey - Expert Fisher and Dumbo - Ninth Wonder of the Universe. 

It's a lot of boxes ticked on a sweet little card. Love it. 

#6 Meilin Lee - Losing Control

I don't think many people are surprised that Meilin Lee - Losing Control has chops. The comparisons to Ariel - Spectacular Singer were not lost on us when she was revealed in Attack of the Vine!. 

That said, I would argue this is still a success story in waiting. While Meilin has seen play in Emerald, Steel and Ruby variants of song decks, none of these have quite managed to break through at the top tournament tables. In my opinion, it's only a matter of time (and maybe a few more cheap songs in Hyperia City) until we really see what she can do. 

#5 Mickey Mouse & Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo

Moving onto perhaps the hottest card of the moment: Mickey Mouse & Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo have seen most of their sales as a late surge after the North American championship. What's got this tag-team so hot, exactly? 

Well, people really got talking after this Emerald Sapphire deck managed to reach the top eight of a 128-player event. This deck is all about shifting an early copy of Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse - Adventuring Duo to quest for buckets of lore, before allowing a near-uncontestable board of Ward characters to sweep up the mess. 

Is it good enough to stick around? I think so. More importantly, the community is snapping up almost every copy they can find at under $3. 

#4 Pocahontas - Guiding the Tribe

Pocahontas is one of the more impressive tools available to the Emerald Amber deck lists featuring Elinor - Renowned Diplomat. After all, what better way to fill out your board the turn before Elinor than dropping bonus extra characters for free?! 

These decks are often pushing 20 one-cost characters, so it's very difficult for Pocahontas - Guiding the Tribe to miss on value before shifting into a back-breaking Pocahontas - Peacekeeper. 

Building a board before protecting it from being challenged? I dunno, that sounds pretty darn good to me. 

#3 Mike Wazowski - Heroic Climber

Speaking of cards that've been earning their keep alongside Elinor, I think we've removed any doubt that Mike Wazowski - Heroic Climber is one of the better early plays in Amber right now. Sure, your opponent has the opportunity to generate card advantage too, but they're not always going to see a character like you will. 

They also can't use any of those cards if you put your foot down and get the game over, so there's that too. 

As far as I'm considered, Mike is one to watch as the format continues to age, and Hyperia City enters the fray. As long as we continue to see a character-heavy aggro deck at the top tables, you'll be seeing plenty of this one on the opposing playmat. 

#2 Gaston - Superior Archer

It's a fall from the throne for Gaston - Superior Archer, who previously held the title as the best-selling card in all of Attack of the Vine!. That said, the fact that Gaston has held onto one of the podium spots since release is one heck of an endorsement for the power level of the card. 

There's plenty of big bads that need to be slain at the top of the format right now, but Gaston really shines in Amber shells packing Support characters like Agustin Madrigal - Exceptionally Kind and Lilo & Stitch - Fun-Loving Friends. In a pinch, you can grant your Support trigger onto an opposing character, giving them enough strength to be brutally struck down. 

This card should be a staple for its entire tenure in Core Constructed, which is still the better part of two years. Grab yourself a foil playset and thank me later. 

#1 Mushu - Stealthy Dragon

Do you know how utterly nuts it is that the most expensive legendary in a set is the best-selling Disney Lorcana card of the month?! It's almost as absurd as the fact that Mushu - Stealthy Dragon is still only sitting at $10 per copy. 

Mushu is one of the fundamental threats of Emerald Steel. It's a must-answer advantage engine that threatens to snowball out of control if left unchecked. I've seen Mushu played in Emerald shells of every color at this stage and I do not expect that to change. To go out on a limb? I think this card is criminally undervalued on account of how many boosters of Attack of the Vine! got opened. 

As we move further from the initial release of the set, that cannot remain true. Mushu has to either fall off in popularity or begin spiralling in price — and I'm putting my money on the latter.

item.title: The Top 5 Most Busted Cards in Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration
item.description:
Pokémon|competitive

The Top 5 Most Busted Cards in Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration

Mew is a total copycat.

By Natalie Millar

|@nataliem9999
|

Published Sep 15, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Hello everyone! 30th Celebration is almost here, and it is very exciting to finally have a unified set release around the world!

While this set doesn't look like it will be extremely impactful, there are still a few solid cards that are looking like they could a small shake up on some of the strong decks.

The Most Busted Cards in 30th Celebration

#5 Ditto

Ditto's Surprisingly Transform attack is a very unique effect. On a heads, you swap your Ditto for a Pokémon in your deck, and keep all the effects and Energy that had been on your Ditto. Notably, Surprisingly Transform does not specify Basic Pokémon, so you can grab Evolution Pokémon straight into play.

The initial hype this card saw was from being able to Crispin onto it and then immediately get a Dragapult ex into play, but I don't really see the vision for this idea since you want to evolve through Drakloak anyway.

Ditto does synergize with Backtrack Badge, and I think it will cause players to look closely at any of the interesting Stage 2 Pokémon that come out in future sets.

#4 Zoroark

Nighttime Byway does not look very appealing, but this Ability has been printed in different forms multiple times in the history of the Pokémon TCG, and it has seen success in various eras. Reducing the Energy for your Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost has a ton of potential (look at how strong Latias ex is).

Zoroark reduces the Retreat of Evolution Pokémon, which could bring a bunch of Stage 1 Pokémon back into the format. It is competing with Air Balloon, which I think will make Zoroark unlikely to see play immediately, but once the "I" block rotates I could see this card getting a massive spotlight!

#3 Espeon

Various Espeon cards in the past have devolved the opponent's Active Pokémon. Espeon-EX from BREAKpoint even had this exact same attack!

The biggest difference between now and 2016 when this old Espeon was released is that there are many more things that you can do now to progress the game without attacking. I could see Espeon ex being played to stall opposing early boards against decks like Dragapult ex, or as a finisher in a Froslass/Mukidori style of deck.

This attack is slightly weaker than Espeon ex's Amazez attack, but it is also significantly easier to power up, and I could see Espeon being played in some slower decks in the future!

#2 Unown

Unown's Mysterious Signal attack is very reminiscent of Iron Hands ex's Amp You Very Much and Stoutland V's Double Dip Fangs, both of which have been mainstays in high tier decks in the past. Taking extra Prize cards upon a Knock Out is a very strong effect, and there are several ways to take advantage of it with our current cardpool.

While 40 damage is not a lot, Budew is a very popular card in Dragapult ex decks and it only has 30 HP. Since Unown is also a Psychic type, it benefits from Telepathic Psychic Energy and Lillie's Clefairy ex's Fairy Zone Ability. With Fairy Zone you take a one-hit KO on Dreepy and take an extra Prize card, progressing well against the most popular deck in the current format.

The main deck I could see Unown seeing play in is the Slowking deck, where they can use Mysterious Signal with Seek Inspiration and already play Wondrous Patch to get extra Psychic Energy into play. Unown also synergises well with Munkidori, which some Slowking players already play because you can move 10 damage over and take the KO on Drakloak. Additionally, you can paralyze an Alakazam with a Drapion then finish it off with Mysterious Signal to take the extra Prize card and jump ahead in one of your tougher matchups.

Unown also synergises well with the next card on this list, and I think they could make a splash at the upcoming Brisbane Regional Championships. 

#1 Mew ex

There have been a ton of Mew cards in the past that have copied attacks, and this new one continues that tradition.

Memory Helix lets you use the attacks of all your Benched Pokémon, you just need the correct Energy for those attacks. This gives you a ton of new options, especially because the Mew ex itself is a Basic Pokémon with free retreat.

The initial deck this card is expected to see play in is Slowking, since it lets you Trifrost with a Basic Pokémon. Part of Dragapult ex's game plan to beat Slowking is to let them Trifrost, then trap the zero-Energy Slowking active and snipe around it with Fezandipiti ex's Cruel Arrow to eventually set up for a six-Prize Phantom Dive while your opponent is helpless. With Mew ex you now force a Boss's Orders for them to trap your Slowking, and if they miss this you can just retreat into Mega Kangaskhan ex and rebuild your hand way faster thanks to the additional cards.

Personally, I am a little skeptical of Mew ex being good in Slowking as that deck already struggles with board management. But I think this card could really shine in the Mega Kangaskhan/Ogerpon deck.

Being able to use Fezandipiti ex's Cruel Arrow into Wellspring Mask Ogerpon ex's Torrential Pump with the same three Energy seems very appealing, especially when your opponent can't respond to it with a Phantom Dive without taking the Knock Out. Mew's attack itself is also not bad. Teleportation Burst takes the Knock Out on Budew then pushes itself back into Mega Kangaskhan, letting you Run Errand again and continue building on your hand.

I think Mew ex is an improvement to the Mega Kangaskhan/Ogerpon deck which already got a Top 8 placement at the World Championships!

item.title: The Top 10 Most Valuable (Non-Serialized) Yu-Gi-Oh Cards in Magnificent Monsters
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|finance

The Top 10 Most Valuable (Non-Serialized) Yu-Gi-Oh Cards in Magnificent Monsters

You can still crack insane cash without a serial number.

By Anthony Tachella

|@tinymech
|

Published Sep 16, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The newest Yu-Gi-Oh! set, Magnificent Monsters, has officially been out for a hot minute now. The crazy thing about this set is that the hype just hasn't died with it. People are still opening up box after box while chasing one of the exclusive Grand Master Rares.

The Most Valuable Cards in Magnificent Monsters

While the Grand Master Rares are the main chases in the set, there are still plenty of non-serialized cards that are valuable and worth opening this set to get. The Grand Master Rares are basically impossible to get, with only 100 copies of each available. You have to be incredibly lucky to pull one. Thankfully, non-serialized versions of all these cards are available.

And they're still very valuable.

In fact, some of the Starlight Rare Extended Art cards in MAMO are pushing and sometimes going over the $1000 mark! Today, we're going to look at the top 10 cards in MAMO. We're going to look past the Grand Master Rares. Since they're more valuable than any other card you could pull… in any pack, really.

#10 Synchro Emergency (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Synchro Emergency is the first card on our list today. Since we're starting here, it's worth noting that market prices for all of these cards aren't a reliable resource. As more packs open every day, more listings pop up, and card values have been shifting faster than market prices can keep up.

Synchro Emergency's Starlight Extended Art print is currently sitting around the $200 mark. Since MAMO became legal, Kewl Tune decks everywhere have been sneaking a set of Synchro Emergency into their Side Decks as a means to allow for additional turn zero plays. This card is typically used as a way to push plays on your opponent's turn, even if you aren't going first. Since it can be activated directly from your hand, there are a ton of applications for this card that make it really good when going second.

Honestly, even after Kewl Tune fades from popularity, I can see this card continuing to be played in Sychro-centric strategies across the board. 

#9 Gagaga Magician - Gagaga Magic (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

One of the most popular Xyz-related strategies recently has been the Onomat archetype. These are the cards that feature the funny names like "Gagaga", "Zubaba", "Dododo", and "Gogogo". The cards have fun names to say, and they're actually a really solid Xyz strategy. Centered around churning out different Rank 4 monsters, the Onomat archetype is incredibly powerful thanks to its toolbox of cards.

This card is really strong and lets you instantly summon itself and any other Onomat monster to make an Xyz Monster that shares a Rank with one of the monster's Levels. Turning two incompatible monsters into a singular Xyz Monster is always a powerful effect, especially when your opponent can't interrupt the middle of your play with something like Book of Moon.

Right now this card is sitting around $235, which isn't bad for a Starlight Extended Art. It also isn't great when you consider we don't have a real idea of how strong this deck actually is for Onomat strategies. Once those decks get a chance to shine in the meta again, I'm sure Gagaga Magician - Gagaga Magic will go up in value. 

#8 Kuriboh - Multiply! (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Kuriboh - Multiply! is only a little more expensive than Gagaga Magician, sitting comfortably around $250. The Extended Art version of this card is just wonderful, and the Starlight Rare looks even better.

Honestly, seeing this card sitting around $250 just feels really low, this card has a ton of potential as more Dark Magician support gets released over the years. 

#7 Winged Kuriboh Sabatiel LV10 (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

HERO lovers rejoice! Wait, this isn't a HERO Monster! It's Winged Kuriboh in an upgraded form! This card is incredibly powerful for HERO strategies and will likely fit itself nicely into the crazy HERO pile decks that you see at your locals. I doubt that this card will be enough to push HERO decks over the edge into the competitive scene, but they're still someone's favorite deck.

This card is sitting right around the $315 mark right now. It has a ton of collectability thanks to it being a Kuriboh card that can be played with HERO decks. You have two super popular archetypes that can work together and keep the value of a card way up there.

#6 Favorite HERO Shining Flare Wingman (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Remember Elemental HERO Shining Flare Wingman? I remember that card. The newest upgraded forms of the HERO monsters are being labeled as Favorite HERO monsters. This card is also just crazy good. It's super generic and works in just about any deck that can Fusion Summon. It only needs a Fusion monster and any other face-up monster on the field.

This card has a ton of potential to make an impact on the competitive metagame. More decks are ending their turns with Fusion monsters on the field, which means that decks are even more susceptible to Super Polymerization than ever before. Most of the listings for this card's Starlight Rare printing are sitting around $375, and I feel like this is easily one of those cards that can only go up over time, especially as people realize how versatile it really is. 

#5 Stardust Dragon - Victim Sanctuary (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

As we break into the top five non-Grand Master Rares, we start hitting the cards that have been consistently over the $500 mark since their release. Of the five cards here, Stardust Dragon - Victim Sanctuary is probably the weakest of them, which is saying something considering it's a Stardust Dragon card.

Victim Sanctuary is really cool because it gives you a free omni-negate that can turn into any Stardust Synchro Monster. The biggest value of this card isn't even its awesome effect, but the fact that it's Stardust Dragon. Being the ace monster of Yu-Gi-Oh 5Ds' Yusei Fudo is certainly a huge factor for collectors. 5Ds has always been one of the more popular series of Yu-Gi-Oh, so having an upgraded version of the protagonist's monster is going to be huge.

#4 Sky Striker Mecha - Widow Anchor (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Alright, here we are getting into the super-playable top-end cards in Magnificent Monsters. Everybody knows how good Sky Striker decks are. Now, Sky Striker has two Extended Art versions of some of their most powerful Spell cards, with Sky Striker Mecha - Widow Anchor always being one of the most important cards in the Sky Striker arsenal.

The Extended Art Widow Anchor is currently sitting at around $85, which isn't too bad for an awesome Extended Art. The Starlight Extended Art, however, is currently $650. That's more than seven times the regular Extended Art version of the card!

#3 Sky Striker Mobilize - Linkage! (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Widow Anchor is a Sky Striker card that has been around since the beginning. Linkage, on the other hand, is a much newer card in the Sky Striker toolbox. It has been a mainstay in Striker decks since its release because it allows for some really creative one-turn kills, as well as pseudo-targeting protection by sending away cards on the field for its effect.

The Extended Art for Linkage is a gorgeous card, just like Widow Anchor. It's currently sitting at around $100, while the Starlight Rare Extended Art is $750. You're looking at over $4000 for just your Linkage and Widow Anchor Starlight Rare Extended Art playsets.

#2 Dark Magical Curtain (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Now, the top two cards… The Yugi cards. In Magnificent Monsters, we have a brand new Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl card. The Dark Magician Girl card isn't even a Monster card! Instead, we have Dark Magical Curtain, which is one of the most hyped up cards in the set for both players and collectors. You have this awesome card with a super cute Dark Magician Girl artwork on it, and you have a recipe for one of the most expensive Starlight Rares around.

Currently, the Starlight Rare for this card is over $1000, which is an insane jump from Linkage's $750. The crazy thing about this card is that it is really good. I mean, like… People are winning regionals with Dark Magician in their decks in 2026. That should say something. Ya, know?

#1 Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant (Starlight Rare) (Extended Art)

Alright, the most expensive (non-serialized) card in Magnificent Monsters is the $1400 Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant. The Starlight Rare Extended of the new Dark Magician card is breathtaking. This card looks absolutely insane. It's essentially the real cover card for the set, even with all the other monsters that are featured on the box art. We all know that the real one you want to pull is this ultimate wizard in terms of attack and defense.

Dark Magician, the Pharaoh's Servant, is also already seeing a ton of play in Light and Darkness Ritual decks. It, alongside Dark Magical Curtain, has revitalized Dark Magician decks as a strategy, and it's really cool to see how much synergy the engine has with some of the top decks in the game right now.

Sure, Grand Master Rares are easily the most expensive and valuable cards in MAMO, with some of the cheapest selling for more than $5,000 at a time. But it's hard to open packs with the realistic mindset of opening one of those cards. Even Starlight Rare Extended Arts are a bit of a stretch, but still significantly easier to pull than a Grand Master Rare. Either way, this set is proving to be one of the most top-heavy sets we've seen in a while. The crazy thing is that this set is still flying off shelves with everyone chasing one of those awesome serialized cards.

item.title: Check Out TCGplayer's EXCLUSIVE Reality Fracture Preview Cards!
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|casual|news

Check Out TCGplayer's EXCLUSIVE Reality Fracture Preview Cards!

Setting the pace of battle has never been easier.

By Emma Partlow

|

Published Sep 17, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Reality Fracture sees the creation of the Echoverse, an alternate existence orchestrated by none other than The Theorist (more commonly known as Jace Beleren) in response to dealing with decades of trauma. It's not the kind of response we're used to when playing Magic: The Gathering, unless you're familiar with Jace, the Mind Sculptor during the Caw-Blade era. Through the incredible story (which I implore you to read if you haven't already, you can do so here), it's created several degrees of "What If" in Reality Fracture — as in, what would happen to some of your favorite characters if the story played out differently?

Despite the dystopian undertones that dwell at Hexhaven University, some of the Echoverse characters come with surprisingly heartwarming stories — such as the Golem who's going to be okay in Karn, Gilded Guardian, to Fblthp who has found his way out of Ravnica and seeking out every crevice of the Echoverse through the Omenpaths instead. Unfortunately, The Theorist also maintains a twisted sense of humor: Gallia, Tragic Host becomes one of the saddest party-goers in the Theran Underworld; along with Mabel, Bitter Recluse of Bloomburrow, who joins the Calamity Beasts to seek revenge against King Glarb. It's not all sunshine and flowers in Reality Fracture though, although it seems Gideon's Memorial is never short of them.

And it's that polarization of characters that's really setting up Reality Fracture to be a memorable experience for players regardless of their tenure and journey into Magic. To add to the incredible flavor beats thus far, I'm thrilled to reveal two exclusive cards from Reality Fracture, which adds to the exciting web of the Echoverse and one you won't want to miss if you're a follower of Amonkhet — let's hit the ground running with Samut, Hazoret's Champion.

Much has happened since the turbulent events of March of the Machine, and Samut was one of many planeswalkers who desparked after the Phyrexian War. Despite losing her spark, she keeps true to her ability of granting other creatures haste, a passive ability that appeared on her first card from Amonkhet in  Samut, Voice of Dissent almost a decade ago. What makes this updated take on Samut so interesting, however, is that she costs only two mana — which I believe is the cheapest haste enabler that specifically calls out only your own creatures to benefit from the ability. Sure, there's Emblem of the Warmind from Future Sight that also does this, but it's an aura and requires some amount of hoop-jumping to really get going. Admittedly Samut's effect isn't anything fancy, it's incredibly efficient in a world where you want nothing more than to rumble into the red zone or activate your creature's abilities as soon as possible.

Expect to see this Samut at the casual Commander tables upon release, and I know I'm already considering her as an addition to Anzrag, the Quake-Mole. As the flavor text implies, Multiverse's Samut charges towards a brighter future as Hazoret's fervent champion, whereas Echoverse's Samut tyrannically rules Naktamun, steering it toward a colder tomorrow.

The Echoverse brings us a more sinister take in Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun — who rules with an icy fist and a chilling demeanor. She wields the ability to slow down time to the point it appears to freeze, keeping her one step ahead of her foes (which interestingly features Hapatra as her feared enemy in this timeline). This is reflected in her card, granting any instant and sorcery spells you cast with split second, as if you're slowing down time yourself. If you've fallen into Magic recently through Universes Beyond or similar and are unfamiliar with split second, then you'll want to know all about it — it's a real doozy of a keyword ability.

Essentially, split second means whenever you cast a spell with the keyword and that spell goes on the stack, players can't cast spells or activate abilities that aren't mana abilities. That overloaded Cyclonic Rift you've just cast? Congratulations! Your opponents can't respond to the spell, but can tap any of their mana creatures in response before you sweep the battlefield away of threats. Or how about you casting a Swords to Plowshares to answer a problematic creature? No problem, as split second guarantees the removal of the creature with Samut in play — leaving your opponents frozen in time as you take control of the battlefield.

Split second is a historically powerful keyword and one that ranks highly on Mark Rosewater's Storm Scale. It's one we don't see often because of the lop-sided gameplay it can create, but it fits rather elegantly in Reality Fracture and will inevitably cause ire at the Commander tables. That said, there's potential for the Tyrant of Naktamun to appear in competitive formats such as Standard Constructed, perhaps opening the door for spell-based archetypes to incorporate a classic keyword such as this one on Reality Fracture release day and beyond.

Reality Fracture releases on October 2, where you can potentially open any of these cards in Play and Collector Boosters, Bundles, Prerelease Packs, Draft Night Boxes, and more. There's also a four-color Commander Deck to support the release, along with five Commander Decks geared towards beginner play under the Magic Foundations name.

Celebrate Usurp The Shadow Throne With TCGplayer's EXCLUSIVE Flesh and Blood Promo Cards

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Sep 17, 2026

|

3 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Everybody likes a bit of bling.  

There's a charm to having something exclusive: a premium product that can sit pride of place as a grail of your collection, or garner compliments and sideward glances when you play it at the table. In a game like Flesh and Blood, players often find themselves so emotionally tied to their choice of hero that these collectibles become more than a showpiece — they're a statement of loyalty.  

I'm an equally guilty partner in this. I pick up almost every souvenir package and tournament pack promo I can get my hands on. TCGplayer editor and all-round fantastic human Peter Day once called me out for it in an article! Simply put, I like to bling out my decks and collection because of where this game has taken me. I love that I can tell the stories of where I've been through beautiful cardboard.  

So, make no mistake... my wallet will be opening up again on September 24th 2026. 

Yup! The team at TCGplayer are partnering up with Legend Story Studios to celebrate the release of Usurp the Shadow Throne. We've got three exclusive extended art rainbow foil promo variants of brand-new cards featured within the set: Blasmophet's Boon, Consuming Command and Goremass Summoning.  

All three of these cards theoretically add a ton of power to fan-favorite monster Levia, Shadowborn Abomination, who is getting more than a fresh lick of paint in Usurp the Shadow Throne. Between them, you're capable of summoning the new Blasmophet, the Insatiable Hunger token, attacking with it (with Go Again) and gaining a consistent boost while it sits in play.  

I'm expecting these to prove very popular with fans of the Shadow Brute, so what exactly will you need to do to get your hands on them?  

When Does The Giveaway Start? What Do I Need to Do?

This promotion will be available for one day only. You'll need to be on the ball on September 24th 2026 between 10:00am ET and 11:59pm ET. At that point, the promos are gone and your purchase will not qualify.  

Eligible buyers will receive one of three promo cards at random:  

  • Blasmophet's Boon (Micro Extended Art Rainbow Foil)
  • Consuming Command (Micro Extended Art Rainbow Foil)
  • Goremass Summoning (Micro Extended Art Rainbow Foil)  

How do you qualify during that window? Simply spend $100 or more (excluding tax and shipping) on the TCGplayer marketplace in a single order. This isn't exclusive to Usurp the Shadow Throne products, so if you've been putting off that beautiful promo card, fancy building a new deck or simply forgot to pick up sleeves during your last trip to the LGS, there's never been a better time to follow through. It all counts, regardless of game. 

I'm probably just buying more Usurp the Shadow Throne though. I have a problem. 

Campaign Eligibility

Time for the "Terms and Conditions" part of the article. I know, I know. It's not the most exciting part — but I prefer to make sure the rules are nice and clear. That way, everybody knows what they need to do to secure their cards and I have less people yelling at me on social media. Win-win.  

  • This promotion is only applicable to purchases made in the United States of America.
  • This promotion is limited to the first 5000 eligible orders during the promotion window.  
  • The promotion window runs exclusively on September 24th 2026 from 10am EST until 11:59pm EST
  • You will receive one of three promo cards at random. You cannot choose or exchange which promo card you receive.  
  • This promotion is limited to once per customer.  
  • This promotion is limited to one per household/address.
  • You cannot purchase additional promo cards as part of this promotion.
  • If you have successfully secured a promo card, you will receive a confirmation email on Monday 28th September 2026.  
  • Shipping will begin Friday, October 2nd 2026. Promo cards will be shipped in a separate package at no additional charge. Tracking is available on request.  

As always, I'm sure I've managed to miss something that should have been in my FAQ. If you have further questions or concerns regarding this promotion, please reach out to our customer support team and they'll take care of you.  

Thanks for reading! May Blasmophet bless you in your quest for whichever promo you're looking for. Just be careful... she's looking awfully hungry these days.

item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Magic: The Gathering This Week - 09/17/2026
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Magic: The Gathering This Week - 09/17/2026

Loyalty pays (especially on the secondary market).

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Sep 17, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

Welcome back, Planeswalkers.

Well, Jace anyway. Reality Fracture previews began this week, and the Jace-centric set that brings an entire "Empower Jace" mechanic is putting planeswalker action front and center in a way not truly done since the iconic War of the Spark in 2019. Along with the "mirrored" version of some very cool cards like Stingcaster Mage and Darklight Phoenix, the set looks to be the most unique set entry of the year, and one that is already driving prices.

Know what's good when we're talking planeswalkers? A planeswalker that can give other planeswalkers its abilities, in particular the ability to +2 immediately. That's powerful on a lot of planeswalker designs and players are already beginning to flock to the Simic 'walker that will undoubtedly fit well into the Jace-centric decks to come.

It's the first time Kasmina, Enigma Sage has been truly relevant. It's been a dollar since it was printed back in 2021's Strixhaven: School of Mages that was well-liked but still overshadowed by lack of paper by events of the time, but Kasmina is not getting its opportunity to shine. The price has climbed from a dollar all the way up to $7, a feat made more possible by the fact that it has no reprints and only one variant printing from Strixhaven (the Borderless printing, which went from $2 to $10 practically overnight).

It was only a matter of time before Ichormoon Gauntlet spiked in price. The planeswalker turbo-powering artifact allows every single planeswalker you have in play to proliferate, which is not only an incredibly popular ability at the Commander table but also one that's enormously potent with planeswalkers. That builds up to the ultimate effect for planeswalker decks: extra turns. Extra activations and extra turns are the secret sauce to making planeswalkers work in a format where not one but three opponents can simply attack them, and Ichormoon Gauntlet is spiking hard right now as early adopters of Reality Fracture start to get their lists in rough order.

Ichormoon Gauntlet climbed this week from $5, more or less where it's been for a year, all the way up to its new $20 price tag post-run on the card. Coming from Phyrexia: All Will Be One, there's not all that many copies of this mythic rare out there in 2026 numbers, and that's why it's spiked so drastically. While the new $20 sticker probably won't hold, I don't think we'll ever see the Gauntlet fall back down to $5 with a reprint.

We take a brief interlude from our weekly Commander check-in to bring the update from the world of 60-card: Modern is everywhere right now. With Magic Spotlight tournaments in both the United States and Australia and then a Regional Championship in the United States, Modern has been in the public eye like it hasn't been for a long time. And while the breakout deck of the Regional Championship in Baltimore was undoubtedly Broodscale Combo (with Blade of the Bloodchief, which has climbed hard over the past month from $4 up to $8), it was not the only green creature combo deck to find success in the Regional Championship.

Devoted Druid Combo took Curtis Lam to second place at the Regional Championship, and has sent the price of at least the Special Guests printing up the card climbing in price. The original Druid was printed in Shadowmoor – playing into the set's theme of -1/-1 counters – and inadvertently became a powerhouse across formats, producing infinite mana anywhere you could find a green deck.
The original Druid was printed at common, but that didn't stop it from reaching a height of almost $10 back in Modern's heyday in 2017. 

Since then, it was reprinted several times and fell all the way down to a low of 50 cents before starting to climb back up in the last year. It's up to almost $2 now, but it's the Special Guests printing from Lorwyn Eclipsed earlier this year that I want to call attention to: it's climbed from $9 a month ago to double that today.

Now, back to the Bears.

This guy has some real staying power. Every week when I look at the data, I see several Bears still climbing in price, well more than a month after the release of The Hobbit. But people really like building Beorn the Fierce, and the Bear price hikes just keep coming.

This week it's Lumra, Bellow of the Woods topping the list, with the mythic rare from Bloomburrow climbing from just over $20 a month ago up to $30 today. Obviously this already carries a substantial price tag and is good in any deck, not just Bears, but at a… bare minimum the shared creature type guarantees Lumra popping up in searches, so this Commander staple is seeing demand despite its high initial price tag.

Argoth, Sanctum of Nature from The Brothers' War jumping from $1 up to $5 over the last six weeks makes some sense – although curiously Titania, Voice of Gaea is flat at $6 – but Words of Wilding? Not one that anyone saw coming, but the ancient Onslaught rare with no reprints has the magic creature type on it, even if the cost of skipping a draw to create a 2/2 Bear is wildly unpowered in any format but certainly Commander. But hey, Beorn does give you extra card draw so I suppose you're at least guaranteed access to a way to trigger the Words. Either way, it's a sign of the times that Words of Wilding is up this week from $3 to somewhere north of $10 for a Near Mint copy.

Finally, let's look at Ganax, Astral Hunter, a Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate standout uncommon that has the quirky "Choose a Background" ability that hasn't exactly been a hit in Commander. But in the case of Ganax, the other words on the card make up for that just fine, as Dragon synergies that also happen to make Treasure tokens are incredibly in right now thanks to the several Smaugs that came in The Hobbit.

Ganax was at bulk prices if you look back at the beginning of 2026, but it had already climbed up to almost a dollar before the Smaugs broke containment. Since then, Ganax, Astral Hunter has climbed from $1 all the way up to $5. Dragons have always been one of Magic's most popular creature types, and it's no surprise that with Smaug to lead the way we're seeing a resurgence of interest in the archetype.

See you next week!

item.title: The 10 Cards Everybody Wants from 30th Celebration
item.description:
Pokémon|collecting

The 10 Cards Everybody Wants from 30th Celebration

Pulls worth celebrating.

By Peter Day

|

Published Sep 15, 2026

|

10 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

It doesn't even feel like hyperbole to call 30th Celebration the most-hyped Pokémon TCG set of all time.

Releasing on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 all across the world, 30th Celebration represents the culmination of an unprecedented year for Pokémon cards. With the popularity of Pokémon cards reaching never-before-seen heights in 2026, 30th Celebration is channeling all of that excitement and expectation into a single expansion. More people are opening Pokémon cards than ever before, and this is the set they most want to rip.

So, which cards are fans hoping to find in 30th Celebration? The honest answer is simply, "all of them." With its tidy set size, historical significance, and seemingly generous pull rates, 30th Celebration practically demands to be collected into master sets containing one of every card in the expansion. Some pulls will be rarer than others, but each one will be a crucial piece in somebody's collection, and every rarity contains cards with special significance.

For example: did you notice that the Rares in 30th Celebration are the 18 Legendary mascot Pokémon from the nine generations of Pokémon games? (With Mew and Mewtwo subbed in for Gen I.)

But it's tough to hold "everything" in your head while you're ripping packs. So to help you organize your Keep and Trade piles this week, we've put together a list of a few extra-special cards that fans are eager to get their hands on. These are the cards that everybody wants from the Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration set.

#10 Unown

The Common-rarity Unown won't be on most collectors' radars. If you're a player though, its Mysterious Signal attack may already be giving you flashbacks to meta-defining cards like Iron Hands ex and Arceus & Dialga & Palkia-GX.

Any Pokémon card that lets you cheat ahead in the Prize trade has a good chance of being busted. Mysterious Signal will have trouble getting there on its own most of the time (though its 40 damage is more than enough to one-shot Budew), but in combination with cards that let you spread damage counters, it can turn around an otherwise unwinnable game.

Keep an eye out for copies of this simple Common as you're ripping packs of 30th Celebration. You may want to keep it for yourself if you like mingo's colorful art, or the way the Unown spell out "anniversary." If not, you can probably find a player at your local game store who'll be happy to trade for it.

#9 The Yuka Morii Item Cards

Since 1998, Morii has set herself apart as a Pokémon card artist by using a unique medium. Instead of illustrating Pokémon, she sculpts them out of clay and photographs them using practical backgrounds, often in nature. 

With over 200 cards to her name, odds are high that you've encountered a Morii card yourself in the wild. But this is her first time lending her beloved style to highly playable Item cards like Poké Pad and Ultra Ball, both of which are basically mandatory to compete in Standard.

Collectors who follow Yuka Morii's work will need all three of these Item cards asap, and more than a few players will want to swap Morii's Item cards into all their decks going forward. Every player who needs a playset creates the same demand as four collectors who want one each, so there's a decent chance that these Item cards will be more valuable than you'd expect. If you're not planning to play with them, it won't be hard to find someone who is.

#8 Every "Pikachu Rare" Pikachu

Every booster pack of 30th Celebration comes with one of 30 unique "Pikachu Rare" cards, each featuring a different artist's take on the world's foremost electric mouse. Because they're numbered out of 30, fans will naturally want to collect 'em all, making them all more valuable by association.

Especially in the early days of 30th Celebration, everyone's first priority will be finding their personal favorite Pikachu Rare. The internet fell in love with OKACHEKE's squishy-cheeked Pikachu early on during the reveals of 30th Celebration, so that one's going to be especially sought-after. But fans may also gravitate toward Pikachu 12/30 by USGMEN, the artist behind Bubble Mew. Or Ken Sugimori's redraw of his iconic Pikachu from Base Set. Or the trippy Pikachu by fan-favorite artist Shinji Kanda.

Whatever Pikachu Rare you pull, it's going to be the exact one someone else is looking for.

#7 The Illustration Rare Legendary Birds

Some of the most desirable Pokémon cards of the 2020s have been connected art cards, where each card forms a piece of a larger illustration. And in 30th Celebration, we're getting a triptych of the most iconic Pokémon trio of all time.

The three Kanto Legendary Birds each have an Illustration Rare in 30th Celebration, which combine to form a colorful cloudscape illustration by mashu, the same artist behind the Bulbasaur connected artwork trio from Mega Evolution. 

Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres have appeared as a connected art trio before, way back in 2009's Supreme Victors. Those are now some of the most valuable cards the legendary birds have ever received, which should give you a good indication of how popular these new connected art cards will be.

#6 Special Illustration Rare Greninja ex

With most modern Pokémon sets, the top of everyone's wishlist is filled with Special Illustration Rares (SIRs), the highest-rarity cards that spotlight each artist's unique style and each Pokémon's unique personality. 30th Celebration includes even more high-rarity prizes to chase than a typical set, but it's still chock-full of gorgeous SIRs that collectors are eager to find.

Other SIRs in 30th Celebration like Sylveon ex might end up carrying a higher price, but the Special Illustration Rare that everybody wants is Greninja ex. Not only has Greninja sneaked its way into the upper echelons of many Pokémon popularity polls, but this card's Stealthy Slash attack can assassinate Benched Pokémon out of nowhere, making this card an exciting find for players and collectors alike.

#5 Classic Collection Gengar (Prime)

Back in 2021, when Pokémon was celebrating its 25th year, the anniversary set Celebrations commemorated that history with a special subset called Classic Collection. This subset consisted of 25 iconic cards from the history of the Pokémon TCG, reprinted in their original style with the 25th anniversary logo.

Five years later, we're getting a new Classic Collection as a 30-card subset in 30th Celebration.

Most of the reprints this time weren't included in the Classic Collection five years ago, so only time will tell which ones end up being the most popular. Will it be the reprint of Shinji Kanda's Magikarp, which outperformed everyone's expectations to become the top chase card in Paldea Evolved? Or the reprint of Shining Celebi, whose original version goes for thousands of dollars?

For my money, we should expect great things from Gengar Prime. Every Gengar card on the market has been on an absolute tear over the past three years, including the original Gengar Prime, which went from $100 at the beginning of 2024 to over $1000 today. Heck, Gengar's so popular that people have tried to sell cards from other games by misidentifying it. No Gengar card can be overlooked in today's market.

#4 Day and Night Special Illustration Rare Pikachu ex

Earlier this year, the internet went a little nuts over Pokémon cards that featured "cameos" by other Pokémon who aren't included in the card's name.

The Pokémon Company sure knows how to please its audience. These two cards represent the entire 30th Celebration set in microcosm, complete with all the big-name Pokémon who're present in the set, and the daytime/nighttime theme that runs through all of 30th Celebration's visuals. With literally dozens of cameos, these SIRs form a natural capstone to 30th Celebration.

But every good concert has an encore, and 30th Celebration has a few chase cards that go beyond the set's "natural" apex.

#3 Classic Collection Charizard

Most of the cards in the 30th Celebration Classic Collection haven't been reprinted since their original set. But one card had to be the exception.

It wouldn't be a Pokémon anniversary set without an homage to [Base Set Charizard](Charizard (BS-4), possibly the most famous trading card in history. Finding (and likely losing) this card sparked a lifelong obsession with Pokémon cards in an entire generation of fans. Decades later, we're still swimming through the wake this card left behind.

Nobody can return to the past, but we can tear open a fresh card wrapper in 2026 and find Mitsuhiro Arita's iconic illustration roaring back at us. No Pokémon fan will want to leave 30th Celebration behind before they've experienced that. 

#2 Futuristic Rare Mewtwo ex

Anniversaries are a time to look forward as well as back. To celebrate what might come in the next 30+ years of the Pokémon TCG, TPCi commissioned famed Japanese artist YOSHIROTTEN to define the look for a new rarity: Futuristic Rare.

(Personally, these don't look very "futuristic" to me. But I appreciate them more with the context of YOSHIROTTEN's 2018 FUTURE NATURE exhibition, which used the extremes of the visible spectrum to explore the theme of "seeing the invisible.") 

Fans have been waiting for these cards since Pokémon Day 2026 in February, before this anniversary set had a name. We don't yet know how hard they'll be to pull, but if The Pokémon Company follows the precedent set by similar one-off rarities like Black White Rare, Futuristic Rares will be extremely scarce—and therefore, valuable.

#1 Futuristic Rare Mew ex

While either of Futuristic Rares in 30th Celebration will be incredible pulls, Mew ex will likely be the more desirable of the two. Part of that comes down to its brighter color scheme, and to the way Mew has come to symbolize "the unobtainable" for Pokéman fans, as the only Gen I Pokémon that couldn't be captured by playing the original video games normally.

It also helps that Mew ex is the strongest new card in 30th Celebration. With its Memory Helix Ability, Mew ex can copy the attacks of any three-Prize Mega Pokémon ex while only giving up two Prizes itself. That's the same kind of Prize-cheating that makes Unown so dangerous, on a Pokémon that can slot easily into decks of any Energy type.

Editor's Note: This article originally ended here, but The Pokémon Company kept one more group of cards a secret until 30th Celebration released. Now that they've been revealed, the cards that everybody most wants from 30th Celebration are...

#0 The Three RGB Mew Cards

Like Mew itself in the original video games, these cards were originally just sketchy-sounding rumors. As early as July, a streamer opening 30th Celebration packs appeared to find a parallel Mew card with art credited to YOSHIROTTEN and a collector number of B/RGB.

This sparked a small firestorm of controversy over whether the card was actually real. Skeptics noted that the card didn't have the 30th Anniversary stamp common to all the other cards in both 30th Celebration and the 30th Celebration Classic Collection.

Now, the skeptics (myself among them) have to eat their words. The number of copies that have been found around the world are too numerous and similar to one another to be faked. While Mew R/RGB, Mew G/RGB, and Mew B/RGB have yet to be added to Pokémon's official card database or 30th Celebration marketing pages, it appears that The Pokémon Company just wants to keep an air of mystery around these exceptionally rare cards.

As Pokémon's best-kept secret in decades, the RGB Mew cards are the ultimate chase cards of 30th Celebration.
